newsitem.title: CANADA: BC Sugar agrees to Onex-backed bid.
newsitem.headline: BC Sugar agrees to Onex-backed bid.

text.p: B.C. Sugar Refinery Ltd said on Thursday it entered into an agreement with BCS Acquisition Inc, an indirect subsidiary of Onex Corp and Balaclava Enterprises Ltd under which BCS Acquisition will make a takeover bid for all the Class A and B common shares of BC Sugar at a price of C$16.50 a share in cash.
B.C. Sugar said its board of directors will recommend the Onex/Balaclava bid to shareholders.
The bid is conditional on having 66-2/3 percent of common shares tendered, including the 20 percent of shares already head by Balaclava.
The agreement would end a long battle for the sugar company by Vancouver businessman Stuart Belkin's Balaclava and Great Pacific Acquisition Inc, representing financier Jim Pattison.

BC Sugar said it was advised by Great Pacific that Great Pacific will extend its June 4 bid and BC Sugar urged its shareholders to use the extension to withdraw any shares already deposited under the Great Pacific bid.

The Onex/Balaclava agreement allows BC Sugar to respond to a superior offer if one is received prior to the expiration of the Onex/Balaclava bid. Onex/Balaclava would have the right to match the superior offer, BC Sugar said.

BC Sugar also agreed that it will pay a break-up fee of C$10 million if the board withdraws its recommendation, if the board fails to reaffirm its recommendation within 48 hours after the announcement of a superior proposal, if a superior proposal is made and the Onex/Balaclava bid is withdrawn, or if 66-2/3 percent of the common shares are not tendered to the Onex/Balaclava bid and another person has acquired sufficient shares to represent de facto control of BC Sugar.
If the Onex/Balaclava bid is withdrawn under certain circumstances and there is no superior proposal it will be paid a break-up fee of C$2 million.
BCS Acquisition Inc will be 75-percent owned by Onex and 25-percent owned by Balaclava. Onex said the bid will be mailed to shareholders by July 7 and expire 22 days later.
Onex said the support of the BC Sugar board of directors confirms that the offer is a clearly superior offer.
"Their support means we can proceed with our offer to all shareholders on a truly friendly basis," Balaclava president Stuart Belkin said.
Great Pacific said an affiliate of the Jim Pattison group of companies intends to tender its 28-percent holding of BC Sugar shares to the Onex/Balaclava offer.

BC Sugar had recommended shareholders accept Great Pacific's most recent bid of C$15 a share in cash or, if the aggregate amount of cash payable is not less than C$83 million, one class A non-voting exchangeable redeemable share of Great Pacific.
The two competing bidders had been topping each other's offers for months.
